title: Slide or Turn? Rigid Body Motion Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A drawer slides out, a fan spins, a wheel rolls down the road. Three different motions, yet two simple ideas describe them all. And when Aarav swings his door, the handle edge travels much farther than a point near the hinge, though both start and stop together. How? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we meet the rigid body and its two basic motions: translation and rotation.

On a live motion notebook, three dots on a sliding book move with the same velocity while their distance-time lines sit on top of each other. Then the same three dots on a swinging door turn through the same angle, and the graph splits: the dot three times farther from the hinge covers three times the distance. A slow-mo replay freezes the door to show the angle theta and the arcs. We write the rules step by step (same velocity in translation, same angle in rotation, s = r theta, speed grows with r), see link by link why a rolling wheel is translation plus rotation, and test it with two pause-and-think questions, including the giant wheel cabin. Then a worked door example, the exam trap about rolling, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
